name: First Wave

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Michael Manson made Mr. Impossible submit to the Tourniquet Crossface; before the bell he had slammed Mr. Impossible's right hand in a locker-room door.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: The Emerald Warrior rolled Teko up after Teko ran head first into the turnbuckles and the steel post.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: Redemption won with the Deliverance Frog Splash after a spear; Lyla's interference backfired.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: Jarod Poe won by disqualification when Dean McQueen hit him with a chair; Poe shrugged the shot off.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: The Jobber won with the Tiger Driver.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: Angel Castillo pinned Steven James with an elbow drop after Gridlock (Raze and Nuke) hit James with a chair; Sly Sterling called the referee over for the count.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: Chris McMillan pinned Hawk McDaniel with a crucifix DDT.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round

matches.finish: Golem won with a tiger suplex with a bridge after a thumb to the eye, then put the Claw on Troy Martinez.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round (main event)

notes: The fed's first broadcast: the first round of the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, posted in eight parts.

name: Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Brett Irvine made Jon Savage submit to the Sign of the Times half crab in his first match for the fed.
matches.stipulation: television title qualifying match

matches.finish: Nick Kurtel won with the Folly, a 450 elbow drop, in his first match for the fed; Xanatos had walked to the ring with a balloon during the match.
matches.stipulation: television title qualifying match

matches.finish: Steven James won with a diving headbutt.
matches.stipulation: television title qualifying match

matches.finish: Troy Martinez made Dean McQueen tap to the Texas Cloverleaf, which he calls the Eradication.
matches.stipulation: television title qualifying match

matches.finish: Michael Manson put The Emerald Warrior in the Tourniquet Crossface and the referee stopped the match when the Warrior's arm dropped for the third time; Manson attacked him before the bell.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, quarterfinal

matches.finish: Jarod Poe won with the Black Circle of Death, an airplane spin into a diamond cutter.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, quarterfinal

matches.finish: Golem won with the Backdrop Driver after a DDT on the floor; Troy Martinez attacked Golem afterward.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, quarterfinal

matches.finish: The Jobber pinned Angel Castillo by hooking both legs with a foot on the rope; afterward the Unholy Alliance threw him through the announce table.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, quarterfinal (main event)

notes: The fed's second broadcast, posted in eight parts: the quarterfinals of the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament and the opening matches toward the television title. Two non-televised matches (Gridlock and the High Plains Drifters against local teams) are reported in the commentary only.

name: Racine Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Chris O'Neill made Hawk McDaniel submit to the Rising, an Asian spike, and kept the hold on after the bell.
Shane Rockwell pinned Dalton Parker with the Final Approach after Britni Kelley took off her top and distracted the referee.
Maelstrom made Jon Savage submit to the Mortal Sin after a Death Valley Driver.
matches.stipulation: If Maelstrom lost he would retire; if Jon Savage lost he would sell snacks at the next Riptide

matches.finish: Steven James pinned Redemption with Lights Out, a reverse TKO, after Redemption was distracted by Angel Castillo and Chris McMillan brawling.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet qualifying match

matches.finish: Angel Castillo pinned Chris McMillan while Sly Sterling held McMillan's foot out of the referee's sight.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet qualifying match

matches.finish: Nick Kurtel pinned Brett Irvine with the Folly after Nuke of Gridlock hit Irvine in the eye with brass knuckles.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet qualifying match

matches.finish: Troy Martinez made The Emerald Warrior submit to the Eradication, a Texas Cloverleaf.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet qualifying match

matches.finish: Golem pinned The Jobber with the Backdrop Driver after The Jobber had knocked the referee down and brought a wrench into the ring; Golem turned the wrench on him.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, semi-final

matches.finish: Michael Manson pinned Jarod Poe after hitting him in midair with a small metal object; The Masked Blazer then ran in, saved Poe from a piledriver on a wheelchair and attacked him.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament, semi-final (main event)

notes: Posted in nine parts: the semi-finals of the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament and the qualifying matches for the Great Lakes Gauntlet.

name: Chi-Town Showdown I

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Chris McMillan pinned The Masked Blazer with a floatover DDT after Jarod Poe dropped Blazer with a DDT on the floor; Poe then put a figure-four headlock on Blazer until he went limp.
Jean Rabesque won with the Figure Four; Chris O'Neill blacked out and the referee counted three. Sean Edmunds attacked Rabesque afterward.

The Jobber made Nick Kurtel submit to the step over toe hold after the Tiger Driver. Troy Martinez had been drawn for The Jobber's next match but could not compete (concussion), so Steven James was drawn instead.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet for the television title (first pairing)

matches.finish: The Jobber fell from the turnbuckle over the top rope and out of the ring, which sends a wrestler to the back of the line; no fall was scored and Steven James stayed in.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet for the television title

matches.finish: Jarod Poe pinned Steven James with the Fading Light, an underhook piledriver.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet for the television title

matches.finish: Jarod Poe pinned Angel Castillo with the Sudden Impact release back suplex off the top rope.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet for the television title

matches.finish: The Jobber pinned Jarod Poe with the Tiger Driver after working over Poe's knee, and became the first television champion.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Gauntlet for the television title (final pairing): the winner became the first Great Lakes Television Champion

matches.finish: Gridlock was counted out after Steven James and Brett Irvine drove them off with chairs; Flatliner eliminated the High Plains Drifters with the Devil's Drop; Kraven and Flatliner then pinned Rocky Wellington of The Movement with the Face-Off. JC, who had paid The Movement to help the Unholy Alliance, was at ringside.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title four-way elimination: the winners became the first tag team champions

matches.finish: Michael Manson won the first Great Lakes Heavyweight Championship: both men's shoulders were down on Golem's tiger suplex, special referee Maelstrom and King Krusher counted different men, and after Manson's dragon suplex from behind King Krusher counted the pin.
matches.stipulation: Final of the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament for the first Great Lakes Heavyweight Championship; Maelstrom was special referee

notes: The fed's first supercard, posted in six parts: the Great Lakes Gauntlet for the first television title, the four-way elimination for the first tag team titles and the final of the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title Tournament for the first Great Lakes Heavyweight Championship.

name: Gary House Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Jon Savage won with the jumping piledriver after sliding down the Warrior's back out of the Torture Rack.
John Skieler and Chris O'Neill brawled on the floor until both were counted out.
The Jobber pinned Chris McMillan with a second Tiger Driver in 16:09.
Rocky Wellington pinned Kurt Rogers with The Process in 7:32.
matches.stipulation: Tag Team Title number one contender's match

matches.finish: Steven James won when Angel Castillo could not rise by the ten count, in 14:06, after punching Sly Sterling.
matches.stipulation: Cuban Death Match (last man standing)

matches.finish: Michael Manson pinned Jarod Poe with Sweet Dreams in 15:02 after The Masked Blazer hit Poe with a loaded headbutt.
matches.stipulation: Grudge match (not for the title)

matches.finish: Kraven and Flatliner pinned Golem with the Devil's Drop in 19:57; afterward Chris O'Neill attacked Golem and Maelstrom and Golem turned on him.
matches.stipulation: Main event tag team match

notes: A house show reported in the short recap format (one post by the announcers, with match times).

name: South Bend Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Jon Savage pinned Steven James with the jumping piledriver after his manager Johnny Wildside grabbed James's leg.
Angel Castillo pinned Brett Irvine, in Irvine's first match since his eye injury, with the Salsa Picante after driving him into an exposed turnbuckle.
Nick Kurtel pinned Nuke with a 450 splash in an upset.

Maelstrom made Chris O'Neill submit to the Mortal Sin; guest referee Michael Manson stalled the count and called the bell only at the end, and Manson and the Unholy Alliance attacked Maelstrom afterward.
Sean Edmunds rolled Troy Martinez up in a small package.
Jean Rabesque pinned John Skieler with a flying crossbody.
Flatliner pinned Rocky Wellington with the Devil's Drop powerbomb and the Unholy Alliance retained.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match

matches.finish: Jarod Poe won by disqualification when The Jobber hit him with a chair; The Jobber kept the title, and The Masked Blazer threw a fireball at Poe afterward.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match

notes: Posted in eight parts.

name: Fort Wayne House Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: The Emerald Warrior made Chris O'Neill submit to the Torture Rack in 6:32.
Jon Savage pinned Entropy with the jumping piledriver in 8:09.
Both teams were counted out in 5:12 after Nick Kurtel's moonsault onto the pile of bodies.
Maelstrom won with the Mortal Sin in 11:13; The Masked Blazer went out.
Jean Rabesque put the figure four on John Skieler and Skieler tapped out in 10:34, after Sean Edmunds hit Rabesque and Troy Martinez with a chair and walked out on Skieler. Rabesque and Martinez won.
The Unholy Alliance pinned Steven James with an inverted Doomsday Device in 9:52 and retained.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match

matches.finish: Golem won in 19:12 when Michael Manson hit him with a steel chair in front of the referee; Manson kept the title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Michael Manson)

notes: A house show reported in the short recap format (one post by the announcers, with match times).

name: Rockford Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Steven James pinned The Emerald Warrior with a snap sleeper neckbreaker; the Warrior was accompanied by Warren Nickolson.
The Masked Blazer drove Brett Irvine face first into the concrete with a piledriver and applied the Demon Storm death grip; Irvine was out and referee Dave Powell called for the bell.
Gridlock, with Sly Sterling, mauled The Movement and pinned Rocky Wellington with the Afterburn in a quick match.
Maelstrom, wearing a bandage from Michael Manson's fire attack, made Chris McMillan submit to the Mortal Sin after a chokeslam onto the turnbuckle; McMillan had hit a floatover DDT and a moonsault.

Jarod Poe, his eyes bandaged after Blazer's fireball, threw salt in Jon Savage's eyes and pinned him with the Sudden Impact release German suplex from the top rope; Poe then hit Johnny Wildside with the Poison Dart.
The Jobber pinned Sean Edmunds with the Tiger Driver after a double clothesline and kept the Television Title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match

matches.finish: Michael Manson rolled Troy Martinez up after ramming his head into a camera, just as Martinez learned that his manager Karen Jewello had been found handcuffed in a boiler room; Manson then piledrove him onto the camera.
matches.stipulation: Non-title match; had Troy Martinez won he would have had a Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match the next week

matches.finish: Referee Al Marinaro ruled a double disqualification because Michael Manson and Maelstrom had come into the ring; while he was down, Golem and Jean Rabesque had made Flatliner tap and pinned Kraven, but the Unholy Alliance kept the titles.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match (champions Kraven and Flatliner)

notes: Riptide in Rockford, posted in eight parts: parts 1, 2 and 6 were first held as cards among the board's earlier threads, and the other five complete the broadcast. Michael Manson's kidnapping of Karen Jewello runs through it and ends in a double disqualification in the tag team main event.

name: Toledo House Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Nikolai Ash pinned The Emerald Warrior with the Lexicon backbreaker in 9:43.
Cameron Cruise won in 10:24 when Johnny Wildside hit him with a shoe and the referee disqualified Jon Savage; Savage and Lyla attacked Cruise after the bell.
Nick Kurtel countered a Raze powerbomb into a hurricanrana package pin in 5:13.
Angel Castillo, with Sly Sterling, stole the three count in 9:34 by grabbing a handful of tights as McMillan tried a victory roll.
Jarod Poe pinned Steven James with the Sudden Impact super German suplex in 14:19.

After Rabesque was knocked down against the exposed turnbuckle and the referee counted to nine, Sean Edmunds knocked the referee out with a right cross; the bell rang at 21:47 and a later broadcast says Edmunds got himself disqualified.
matches.stipulation: Taped Fist Match: the winner had to knock the other out for ten seconds

matches.finish: Maelstrom and Golem won in 27:01 when Maelstrom locked the Mortal Sin on The Masked Blazer and he tapped out; Jarod Poe had attacked Blazer before the bell.
matches.stipulation: Texas Tornado, no disqualifications

notes: A house show reported on the fed's recap show, with Tony Ross and Rick Wiseman introducing video clips of each match and its time.

name: Saginaw House Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Both men used the ringside furniture on each other and the match ended in a double disqualification in 9:36.
Stephen Morgan pinned Cameron Cruise with a snap cradle piledriver in 8:57 after kicking him in the gut.
Steven James slipped out of a body slam and rolled John Skieler up in 9:51; Skieler threw him into the ring steps afterward.
Jon Savage pinned Rychard Isaac, in Isaac's debut match, with the jumping piledriver in 6:58.
Golem pinned Angel Castillo with the Backdrop Driver in 12:25 after knocking Sly Sterling off the apron.

Nikolai Ash won by countout in 18:31 after Michael Manson hit Maelstrom with the ring bell and a German suplex on the floor; Maelstrom put the Mortal Sin on Ash afterward until security pulled him off.

Michael Manson made The Jobber tap to the Tourniquet Crossface in 16:10 after putting a Masked Blazer mask on The Jobber's face backwards; Maelstrom, Kraven, Flatliner, Golem and Jean Rabesque brawled after the match.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Michael Manson; The Jobber was the Television Champion)

notes: A house show reported in the short recap format by the president, with match times.

name: Kalamazoo Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: The Emerald Warrior, with Warren Nickolson, pinned Chris McMillan with a sunset flip as McMillan, slowed by old injuries, put his head down.
Sean Edmunds pinned Nick Kurtel with the Northern Lights Suplex after locking the figure four on him; Edmunds then challenged Jean Rabesque on the microphone and Rabesque hit his knee with a chair.

Flatliner, who had faked a knee injury and hit Rabesque with his knee brace before the bell, pinned Jean Rabesque with the Flatline Heart Punch into the Devil's Drop powerbomb after Kraven hit Rabesque in the head with the ring steps while the referee was warning Flatliner.
Nikolai Ash pinned Cameron Cruise after a low blow the referee did not see, as Cruise held him in the cradle for the Shipwreck.
Maelstrom made Angel Castillo tap to the Mortal Sin after a jackknife powerbomb on Sly Sterling, whose interference had nearly cost Maelstrom the match.
The Jobber made Steven James tap to a step over toe hold after working over his right knee, and kept the Television Title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match

matches.finish: Michael Manson pinned Golem with the Sweet Dreams stunner to keep the title, after Golem had pinned Jarod Poe with a tiger suplex; Manson had thrown salt taped to a chair into Golem's eyes, and Maelstrom had tied up Tempest backstage.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title triple threat match (champion Michael Manson)

notes: Riptide in Kalamazoo, posted in seven parts: the last Riptide before Massive Assault, with Michael Manson locked in a backstage room by King Krusher for most of the show.

name: Massive Assault 2002

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Stephen Morgan made Jon Savage submit to the Stupendous Death Lock, a sharpshooter.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, shown in highlights

matches.finish: The Cannonball Kidd pinned Chris O'Neill with a German suplex after O'Neill charged into the turnbuckle; Kidd had offered O'Neill his help before attacking him.
Nikolai Ash pinned Brian Lawler with the Lexicon, a double underhook powerbomb onto his knee, after Stephen Morgan hit Lawler with the ring bell hammer while Ash had the referee's attention.
Jarod Poe opened The Masked Blazer's eye with the piercings on his hands and pinned him with a Sudden Impact release suplex through a table.
matches.stipulation: Detroit Street Fight

matches.finish: Kraven and Flatliner threw Xanatos out of the ring and pinned Nick Kurtel with the Face-Off to keep the titles.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match

matches.finish: Raze and Nuke pinned Cameron Cruise with the Afterburn; Sly Sterling was with Angel Castillo and Gridlock.
matches.stipulation: Six-man tag team match

matches.finish: The Jobber won two falls to one: he rolled Golem up with a handful of tights for the first, Golem pinned him with a small package for the second, and The Jobber took the third with the Tiger Driver to keep the Television Title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match, best two out of three falls

matches.finish: Jean Rabesque won after driving a jagged piece of the broken table into Edmunds' forehead and hitting him with the microphone until Edmunds said 'I quit'; Edmunds had come close to winning earlier with a Northern Lights Suplex through the table.
matches.stipulation: I Quit match

matches.finish: Maelstrom won the Great Lakes Heavyweight Championship: after breaking the Tourniquet Crossface he hit a chokeslam, a savate kick and the Mortal Sin, and referee Al Marinaro raised Manson's arm three times without a response. Anarky then attacked Maelstrom with a roll of nickels.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title covered steel cage match (champion Michael Manson)

notes: The fed's second supercard, posted in eight parts on 22 January 2003: Maelstrom took the Great Lakes Heavyweight Championship from Michael Manson in the main event and Anarky made his debut afterward.

name: Hammond House Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Jared Justice pinned Angel Castillo, in his GLCW debut, with the Hammer of Justice off the top rope in 8:47.
Rahul Seth rolled Ryan Youngblood up in 6:59 after Spider Murphy hit Youngblood with a foreign object; both teams were making their debut.
Larry Tact pinned Nemesis in 19:17 when Nemesis's superplex attempt ended with Tact falling on top of him; both were making their GLCW debut.
The Cannonball Kidd pinned Golem with the Crater Creator in 10:35 after Golem twisted his knee.
Sean Edmunds, bandaged after the I Quit match, rolled back into the ring and Jarod Poe was counted out in 7:44.
Raze and Nuke pinned Nikolai Ash with the Afterburn in 8:02.
Anarky pinned Steven James with the Chaos Breaker in 7:26 in his GLCW debut.
Maelstrom kicked The Jobber into the turnbuckles as he set up the step over toe hold and made him submit to the Mortal Sin in 11:05.
matches.stipulation: Non-title match: Great Lakes Heavyweight Champion Maelstrom against Television Champion The Jobber; had The Jobber won he would have had a title shot at the next Riptide

matches.finish: Flatliner pinned Brian Lawler, who had hurt his leg falling off the apron, with the Devil's Drop powerbomb in 15:53; Maelstrom made the save for Rabesque afterward.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match (champions Kraven and Flatliner)

notes: A house show reported in the short recap format by the president, with match times.

name: Cleveland Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Shane Rockwell pinned Spider Murphy with the Final Approach, a Death Valley Driver out of an airplane spin.
Stephen Morgan rolled Angel Castillo up after pulling him in front of the powder Sly Sterling threw.
Anarky pinned Rychard Isaac with the Chaos Breaker, his first in-ring appearance on a Riptide.
Nemesis pinned The Cannonball Kidd with the Penance, a cradle brainbuster; Sean Edmunds attacked Nemesis with a tire iron afterward.
Raze and Nuke, with Sly Sterling, pinned Steve Slayer with the Afterburn.
Larry Tact won when Jared Justice lit a blowtorch and referee Al Marinaro disqualified him.
Jarod Poe pinned The Jobber with a Sudden Impact release suplex off the top rope and won the Television Title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match

matches.finish: Michael Manson hit Maelstrom with what looked like brass knuckles and pinned him with the Sweet Dreams stunner while Flatliner had knocked Rabesque off the apron.
matches.stipulation: Six-man tag team main event (Maelstrom was the Great Lakes Heavyweight Champion)

notes: Riptide in Cleveland, posted in eight parts: the first Riptide after Massive Assault, with Jake Shades beside Tony Ross and Rick Wiseman at the announce table.

name: Green Bay House Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: The opening match ended in a double countout of both teams in 3:58 after wild action.
Ryan Roberts pinned Brian Lawler with the Genocide cradle brainbuster in 6:18; Lawler could not get past his knee injury.
Jared Wells beat Jon Savage with the Rage Drop in 8:43 in his in-ring return; Johnny Wildside's interference and Savage's dirty tactics did not save Savage.
Shane Rockwell pinned Raze after the Final Approach in 3:15.

Stephen Morgan pinned Nemesis with the snap cradle piledriver in 26:32 after a drop toe hold sent Nemesis face first into the steel steps and opened him up; Morgan had also hit him with a chair and a referee count had been suspect earlier.
The match went to the 30:00 time limit; the two kept trading amateur wrestling holds after the bell.
matches.stipulation: Non-title match, signed before Jarod Poe won the Television Title

matches.finish: Nikolai Ash pinned Jared Justice with a sunset flip in 13:10 after Justice blocked the Lexicon and flipped him; Justice then tore turnbuckle pads off and threatened the referee.
Anarky pinned Golem with the Chaos Breaker in 14:52 after working over Golem's neck; Michael Manson watched from ringside and Golem had rejected his offer before the match.

Maelstrom kept the title in 26:33, pinning Michael Manson after a chokeslam off the turnbuckle and a second jackknife powerbomb; Jean Rabesque and Sean Edmunds had brawled out into the stands, and Golem chased Anarky from ringside.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title four-way match (champion Maelstrom)

notes: A house show reported as the fed's first online broadcast, with Tony Ross and Rick Wiseman telling each match and its time from clips: the first edition of the program later called Wired. The announced lineup is on the fed's board; a four-way Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match closes the card.

name: Milwaukee Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Ryan Youngblood pinned Spider Murphy with the Blood Drive powerslam after taking Murphy's steel chair from him and hitting him with it while the referee was distracted.
matches.stipulation: Dark match before the broadcast, told by the announcers

matches.finish: Steven James pinned Jon Savage with a snap sleeper neckbreaker out of a rapid reversal sequence.
matches.stipulation: Dark match before the broadcast, told by the announcers

matches.finish: Suicide pinned Ryan Roberts with the Screwdriver, a vertical suplex into a piledriver, after Roberts had slipped out of an earlier Screwdriver and nearly won with a small package.
The referee ruled a double countout as Minion and Nemesis fought their way up the aisle to the back.

Nikolai Ash hit Harold Haggler with the Lexicon powerbomb after Stephen Morgan had dropkicked Haggler into the referee and hit Alex Hand with a chair; Morgan dragged the knocked-out referee over for the three count.

Jarod Poe kept the Television Title, pinning Sean Edmunds, who was favouring his back after Nemesis's attack, with the Poison Dart after Edmunds had nearly won with a roll-up; Larry Tact then hit Poe with a chair.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match (champion Jarod Poe)

matches.finish: The Cannonball Kidd rolled Jared Wells up as Wells charged into the corner, with his feet on the second rope for leverage, and the referee counted three; Kidd ran to the back with Wells chasing him.
Anarky pinned Jared Justice with the Chaos Breaker after Michael Manson, with an official of the Milwaukee fire department at ringside, distracted Justice; Manson and Anarky then beat Justice down.
Kraven and Flatliner hit the Face Off on Shane Rockwell and Flatliner made the pin to keep the Tag Team Titles.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match (champions Kraven and Flatliner)

matches.finish: Jean Rabesque rolled through The Jobber's roll to win a crossbody pin and become the number one contender; The Jobber's foot was on the ropes but referee Al Marinaro did not see it. Michael Manson and Rabesque then brawled at ringside.
matches.stipulation: Main event to name the number one contender for the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title

notes: Riptide in Milwaukee, posted in eight parts: the fed's first show in a major league arena, with two dark matches before the broadcast, the debut announcement of Jonathan Marx and a main event to name the number one contender for the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title.

name: Flint Wired

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Jonathan Marx made Ryan Roberts submit to the STF in 4:21.
Chris McMillan pinned Alex Hand with the floatover crucifix DDT in 5:26; the win put the Dogs of War third in the rankings.
Minion pinned Suicide with the Redemption in 13:31.
Anarky won by disqualification in 14:11 when Jared Wells punched the referee; Anarky hit Wells with the Chaos Breaker afterward.
Michael Manson pinned Jared Justice in 13:09 after hitting a piledriver on Justice onto a stop sign.
matches.stipulation: No disqualification match

matches.finish: Jon Savage pinned Golem with the jumping piledriver in 4:52; Golem, hurt in the parking lot before the show, went to the ring against doctor's orders and briefly got the Claw on Savage twice.
matches.stipulation: Six-man Gauntlet match for a Television Title shot (first pairing)

matches.finish: Steven James pinned Jon Savage with the snap sleeper neckbreaker in 10:19 and advanced to the third round.
matches.stipulation: Six-man Gauntlet match for a Television Title shot

matches.finish: Steven James sent Stephen Morgan over the top rope in 12:19, which under the match's rules slots a wrestler at the back of the line; no fall was scored and James stayed in.
matches.stipulation: Six-man Gauntlet match for a Television Title shot

matches.finish: The Cannonball Kidd pinned Steven James with the Crater Creator 450 splash in 15:27.
matches.stipulation: Six-man Gauntlet match for a Television Title shot

matches.finish: Nemesis rolled up the Cannonball Kidd in 21:03 while Kidd was arguing with the referee over a two count.
matches.stipulation: Six-man Gauntlet match for a Television Title shot

matches.finish: Nemesis pinned Stephen Morgan with the Wrath Uranage Slam in 27:54 to win the Gauntlet; Minion attacked Nemesis afterward and Jarod Poe made the save.
matches.stipulation: Six-man Gauntlet match for a Television Title shot (final pairing): the winner became the number one contender for the Television Title

matches.finish: Kraven and Flatliner hit the Devil's Drop powerbomb and Flatliner made the pin in 11:17 to keep the Tag Team Titles.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match (champions Kraven and Flatliner)

matches.finish: Jarod Poe pinned Larry Tact with the Fading Light screwdriver in 18:37 to keep the Television Title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match (champion Jarod Poe)

matches.finish: Maelstrom pinned Nikolai Ash in 26:53, flipping him with a back body drop and holding Ash's shoulders and arms down with his knees and arms, after Ash had used a mule kick low blow; Anarky and Michael Manson then beat Maelstrom down until Rabesque, Kraven and Flatliner, Justice and Poe made it an eight-man brawl.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Maelstrom)

notes: The first edition of Wired, the fed's online program, recapped by Tony Ross and Rick Wiseman from match clips with times: Golem is found beaten in the parking lot before the show, a six-man Gauntlet names the number one contender for the Television Title and Maelstrom defends the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title against Nikolai Ash.

name: Indianapolis Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Sane pinned Steven James with a jumping DDT after twisting out of James's snap sleeper neckbreaker; his two valets, Kodi Pendant and The Other Girl, fought each other at ringside and in the ring afterward.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, shown in highlights

matches.finish: Jon Savage pinned Alex Hand with the jumping piledriver; Savage had revealed his partner to be his identical twin brother Ric, and the brothers changed places during the match.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, shown in highlights

matches.finish: Jonathan Marx beat Billy Matthews after working over his knee: Matthews rolled him up, Marx reversed it and the referee counted three over Matthews's claim that he had kicked out.
Jason Payne pinned Steven Slayer with a Full Nelson Slam after Chris McMillan's tornado DDT; Ryan Youngblood was too slow to save.
Nemesis pinned The Jobber with the Wrath after Minion had hit The Jobber with the Redemption on the concrete and left him dazed.
Referee David Gross rang the bell and ruled a double countout as four men brawled up the aisle: Jared Wells had gone after Larry Tact and Steven James had called The Cannonball Kidd out of the ring.
Jared Wells pinned Minion with a back suplex into a bridge off the second turnbuckle after Minion turned to shout at Nemesis, who was being held back by security on the ramp.
Stephen Morgan pinned Suicide with the cradle piledriver after kneeing him in the groin as Suicide set up the Suicidedriver.

Anarky pinned Jarod Poe with the Chaos Breaker after kicking him in the groin; Jean Rabesque had been arguing with referee Al Marinaro on the outside, and after the pin he threw Anarky and Michael Manson out of the ring.
matches.stipulation: Part of the double main event

matches.finish: Maelstrom pinned Kraven after catching him in mid-air off the top rope with a powerslam, as Jared Justice and Flatliner brawled out of the ring; Kraven then kneed Maelstrom out of the ring and the four fought up the aisle to the locker rooms, where Michael Manson and Anarky joined the Unholy Alliance and wrapped a plastic bag around Maelstrom's head until Jarod Poe and Jean Rabesque arrived.
matches.stipulation: Non-title match, the second half of the double main event

notes: Riptide in Indianapolis, posted in eight parts: the fed's first trip to the city, with two non-televised matches shown in highlights, the new referee David Gross and a double main event of tag team matches before WarGames.

name: Duluth Wired

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Golden Hawk won in 3:56 with the Lone Star Jam legdrop in his debut.
Martial Law won in 10:13 with Steve Slayer's Slayer Spring Splash after Jon Savage's missile dropkick hit his own partner Ric.
Suicide won in 7:34 with the jumping Suicidedriver.

Anarky pinned Jonathan Marx with the Chaos Breaker after M.W. Grossard jumped the barrier and hit Marx with a DDT on the concrete while Anarky distracted referee Al Marinaro; Marx had nearly won with the STF.

Michael Manson pinned Jared Wells with the Sweet Dreams stunner in 12:02: Wells had hit the Rage Drop and was counted a winner until the referee saw Manson's foot on the rope, and the match was restarted.
The match went to the 30:00 time limit after the two went hold for hold and counter for counter.
Jarod Poe kept the Television Title in 21:02 when Minion hit Poe with a chair and the referee disqualified Nemesis.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match (champion Jarod Poe)

matches.finish: Maelstrom kept the title in 18:35: after the Mortal Sin the referee raised Stephen Morgan's arm three times, it dropped each time, and he called for the bell; Michael Manson and Anarky, who had walked out on Morgan, then attacked Maelstrom until Jean Rabesque ran down.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Maelstrom)

notes: Wired recapped by Tony Ross and Rick Wiseman from match clips: the fed's first trip into Minnesota, a prelude to Ringlords I, with Golden Hawk's debut, a time-limit draw between Jean Rabesque and Nikolai Ash and both singles titles on the line.

name: Ringlords I

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: The Cannonball Kidd pinned Steven James with a spinning heel kick, the Life Turnaround, off the ropes, then knocked James out with a roundhouse kick and hit the Crater Creator on him; Lincoln Jones made his debut by chokeslamming Kidd out of the ring and carrying James to the back.
Nikolai Ash pinned Suicide with the Lexicon powerbomb onto his knee after a missile dropkick; Suicide, who barely fought back, was taken out on a stretcher.
Nemesis pinned Minion with a moonsault off a fire escape onto a car after Minion's own fall from the fire escape onto the hood missed Nemesis; both men left in ambulances.
matches.stipulation: Falls count anywhere in the Twin Cities

matches.finish: Referee Al Marinaro signalled for the bell as The Jobber stayed outside past the ten count, a double countout: Golden Hawk had flipped The Jobber through the ropes and tried a superplex off the safety barrier, which The Jobber flipped through to hit the Tiger Driver in the first two rows, and the two then brawled in the stands.

Jonathan Marx locked M.W. Grossard in the STF until Grossard was out and the referee called for the bell; both men were bloody, and Grossard, his arm already hurt, had missed an elbow drop from the top.

Alex Hand pinned Steven Slayer with a small package to eliminate Martial Law first; Jon Savage then pinned Harold Haggler after Ric Savage's spike piledriver off the second rope, though Ric was the legal man, to eliminate the Oak Street Beach Patrol; Chris McMillan pinned Jon Savage with a floatover crucifix DDT after a blind tag, and the Dogs of War became the number one contenders for the Tag Team Titles.
matches.stipulation: #1 contenders four-way tag team match

matches.finish: Stephen Morgan pinned Billy Matthews with the cradle piledriver after Matthews dived over the ropes and hit the railing throat first; Matthews was helped out by trainers.
Jared Wells hit the Rage Bomb and the referee counted ten over Larry Tact, who reached his knees but not his feet.
matches.stipulation: Lights Out match

matches.finish: Kraven submitted to Jean Rabesque's figure four and Maelstrom's Mortal Sin applied together, after Michael Manson's black mist, meant for Rabesque, hit Kraven and Jarod Poe knocked Manson out with Manson's own metal plate; afterward a hooded man revealed as Dakota Smith, with Nevada Smith at ringside, joined the Unholy Alliance and attacked Manson and Anarky.
matches.stipulation: WarGames: The Match Beyond, a two-ring cage match, four men a side

notes: The fed's first pay-per-view, Ringlords I: Minnesota Mayhem, posted in nine parts: Lincoln Jones's debut, a falls-count-anywhere match through the Twin Cities, a four-way tag team match for the number one contendership, Wells against Tact in a Lights Out match and the WarGames main event.

name: Columbus Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Cameron Cruise rolled up Jared Justice from behind for the three count after Justice ran chest first into the turnbuckle, in Cruise's first match since his hiatus.
Jon Savage pinned Alex Hand with the jumping piledriver while Ric Savage and Johnny Wildside worked Harold Haggler over on the outside.

M.W. Grossard pinned Steven James with a rolling reverse powerbomb when James went for a back body drop, then locked him in a bow-and-arrow hold after the bell; he let go when Lincoln Jones ran in, and Jones threw him out of the ring.
Stephen Morgan pinned Jarod Poe after a stun gun across the top rope, with both feet on the middle rope for leverage while the referee did not see it, and became the new Television Champion.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match (champion Jarod Poe)

matches.finish: Golden Hawk and Sane swung the ring bell and its hammer, then steel chairs from the announce table, at each other, and the referee called for the bell and ruled a double disqualification.
The match ended in a double countout when all four men brawled up the ramp past referee Al Marinaro's ten count.

Anarky won in the end: Nemesis threw Nikolai Ash out, Kidd threw Nemesis out, Michael Manson pulled the top rope down and sent The Jobber out, Wells clotheslined Jonathan Marx out, Anarky threw Kidd out, Maelstrom's interference let Wells send Manson over the top, and Anarky hit the Chaos Breaker on Wells and threw him out.
matches.stipulation: Eight-man over-the-top-rope battle royal for the number one contendership to the Great Lakes Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Maelstrom kept the title with the Mortal Sin after a Jacknife powerbomb: referee Al Marinaro raised Rabesque's arm three times and it dropped each time, and the two shook hands afterward.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Maelstrom)

notes: Riptide in Columbus, posted in eight parts: the first broadcast after Ringlords I, with Cameron Cruise back from his hiatus, a fire trap in Jared Justice's dressing room, a first letter and a video from the stalker who is after Jarod Poe, the Television Title won by Stephen Morgan, an eight-man battle royal to name the number one contender and Maelstrom's first singles match with Jean Rabesque. The Unholy Alliance hands the Tag Team Titles to King Krusher and retires before the main event.

name: Akron Wired

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Lincoln Jones pinned Raizzor with a choke slam in 5:12 in the first match of Steven James and Jones as a team.
The Jobber made Scotty Sanders submit in 6:12 with a Tiger Driver into a step-over toehold on the leg he had worked over.

M.W. Grossard pinned Jared Justice in 7:09 with the Flame Thrower across the top rope after a low blow, struck when the referee had been knocked down in a three-man collision, with Bostwick B. Maximized at ringside.
Shane Rockwell pinned Jon Savage with the Final Approach off the top rope in 4:42 while Britni distracted Savage on the turnbuckle.

Anarky pinned Cameron Cruise with the Chaos Breaker in 16:22, out of nowhere after Cruise missed a second top-rope move; Anarky had kicked open a gash on Cruise's forehead, and Cruise kicked out of a full nelson slam, a cradle piledriver and Anarky's pins in between.
Michael Manson pinned Golden Hawk with the Sweet Dreams stunner in 11:02 after Jonathan Marx rang the bell at ringside and distracted Hawk.
Dakota Smith pinned Jonathan Marx in 12:19 with a swinging spinebuster; Manson, Marx and Anarky then attacked Dakota and Nevada Smith until Maelstrom and Rabesque cleared the ring.

The Cannonball Kidd pinned Jarod Poe in 9:33: Kidd threw the referee into Poe, and a large man in face paint, the Man of Action whom the roleplays name Joe Clarke, came from the crowd, speared Poe, gave him a cradle inverted powerbomb and dragged Kidd on top of him.
matches.stipulation: Booked as a Television Title match before Stephen Morgan won the title at Riptide

matches.finish: Nikolai Ash tapped out to Maelstrom's Mortal Sin in 14:22 after Maelstrom threw him into Stephen Morgan; Anarky, Manson and Marx attacked the winners afterward.

notes: Wired recapped in one post, with each match told with its time: the first match of Steven James and Lincoln Jones as a team, Cameron Cruise's match with Anarky in his return, Dakota Smith's win over Jonathan Marx, the first appearance of the Man of Action and a main event of Maelstrom and Jean Rabesque against Nikolai Ash and the Television Champion.

name: Wisconsin Dells Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Ric Savage pinned Thunderbolt with the jumping piledriver in 7:02 after Johnny Wildside had hit Thunderbolt with a steel chair in the debut match of Black Heart and Thunderbolt.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, shown in a recap

matches.finish: Scotty Sanders pinned Jared Justice with a crucifix in 10:02 when Justice ran chest first into the turnbuckle.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, shown in a recap

matches.finish: The Jobber made Cameron Cruise submit to the step-over toehold after a Tiger Driver and a long attack on Cruise's legs.
Golden Hawk pinned Minion with a mid-air powerslam as Minion went for the Fall From Grace; Jonathan Marx and Minion attacked Hawk afterward until Dakota Smith came to his aid.
Larry Tact pinned Jarod Poe after the Humbling, a uranage, in a match in which each man accused the other of carrying a weapon and Tact threw Poe a chair that Poe dropped.
M.W. Grossard pinned Jared Wells after an elevated DDT; Wells had come to the ring disguised as a woman and attacked Grossard first, having been pepper sprayed backstage by Abby the Nazi.
Shane Rockwell pinned Jason Payne with the Final Approach, an airplane spin into a Death Valley driver, and The Movement became the new Tag Team Champions; Major Impact attacked them afterward.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Tag Team Title match for the vacant titles

matches.finish: Jonathan Marx pinned Dakota Smith with the gourdbuster while Jean Rabesque was still the legal man, after Manson had pulled Jake Shades in front of Rabesque; Nevada Smith and Rabesque argued with referee Al Marinaro afterward.

Nemesis hit the Wrath and covered Morgan, but Larry Tact and Jarod Poe, brawling, knocked him off at one, and the referee called for the bell as the brawl spread to the Cannonball Kidd and Joe Clarke; Morgan kept the Television Title.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match (champion Stephen Morgan)

matches.finish: Maelstrom, whose knee Anarky had struck with a baseball bat before the bell, kept the title with the Mortal Sin, applied from behind after Joe Clarke tried to hand Kidd the belt, and the referee raised Kidd's arm three times; Anarky, Manson, Marx and Minion then beat Maelstrom down.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Maelstrom)

notes: Riptide in an outdoor park on the Wisconsin river, the fed's first outdoor event, posted in eight parts: the debut of Southern Thunder, a stalker's package for Jarod Poe, Grossard's match with Wells in a disguise, the vacant Tag Team Titles won by The Movement, a tag match in which Jonathan Marx pinned Dakota Smith while Jean Rabesque was the legal man, a Television Title match thrown out in a brawl and a main event in which Anarky struck Maelstrom's knee with a baseball bat before the bell and Maelstrom still beat the Cannonball Kidd.

name: Joliet Wired

date.source: The board's own post date of the results.

matches.finish: Yuji Yamashita made Scotty Sanders submit to the Scorpion Fire Deathlock, a reverse Texas cloverleaf, in 8:27 in his GLCW debut.
Jon Savage pinned Steven James with the jumping piledriver in 9:40 after James missed the Soaring Eagle off Lincoln Jones's shoulders.
The Jobber rolled up Dakota Smith in 7:52 and hooked the tights for leverage; Nevada Smith chased him out of the ring afterward.
M.W. Grossard won by disqualification in 14:45 when Jean Rabesque hit him in the nose with the vice grips Abby the Nazi had thrown into the ring.
Larry Tact pinned Jarod Poe with the Point Blank superkick in 12:01; Jared Justice attacked Tact with a chain afterward and opened him up.
matches.stipulation: Texas Tornado match

matches.finish: Anarky pinned Black Heart with the Chaos Breaker in 15:37 after Manson's Sweet Dreams stunner; Anarky then handcuffed Golden Hawk to the guardrail and hit him with a chair while Manson held security off with another.
matches.stipulation: Six-man match

matches.finish: Stephen Morgan pinned Jared Wells in 12:52 after M.W. Grossard slid under the apron and held Wells' legs down.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Television Title match (champion Stephen Morgan)

matches.finish: Maelstrom kept the title in 18:43: his Mortal Sin made the referee raise Marx's arm three times; Manson, Anarky and Minion attacked him until Golden Hawk came in with a chair, and Maelstrom put Anarky out with the Mortal Sin.
matches.stipulation: Great Lakes Heavyweight Title match (champion Maelstrom)

notes: Wired recapped in one post with each match's time: Yuji Yamashita's debut, a Texas Tornado match, a six-man match in which Golden Hawk and Southern Thunder faced Manson, Anarky and Minion, a Television Title match and a main event in which Maelstrom beat Jonathan Marx with the Mortal Sin, with the whole stable at ringside, and then put Anarky out with it.

name: Champaign Riptide

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Steven James pinned Jack Jensen with the Soaring Eagle off Lincoln Jones's shoulders after Jones had dominated the Danish team.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, told in a summary

matches.finish: Jared Justice pinned Yuji Yamashita with the flying hammer elbow drop off the top rope after a powerslam, a DDT, a lariat and a cradle piledriver.
matches.stipulation: Non-televised match, told in a summary

matches.finish: Joe Clarke pinned Ric Savage with the Louder Than Words powerbomb after Clarke had cleaned house on both Savages and Johnny Wildside; Kidd pulled him off Major Impact afterward.

Larry Tact made Cameron Cruise submit to the Tactful Surrender after working over Cruise's back; Jared Justice attacked Tact on the ramp afterward and came after him in the ring with a blowtorch until security held him back.

The Jobber pinned Nemesis with a Tiger Driver on top of the choke slam Joe Clarke had given him while the referee did not see it; Nemesis challenged Kidd to a lumberjack match at the next pay-per-view afterward.
Jared Wells pinned Minion with the Rage Bomb after Jarod Poe's music played with no Poe, and Minion, who had gone for the Fall From Grace, looked for him.

notes: The fed's last Riptide, posted in four parts on 15 October 2003 after the fed had closed, half a card written a month earlier by one of its two card writers: the announcement of WrestleBowl I, Minion's attack on Jarod Poe in the parking lot, Cameron Cruise's match with Larry Tact and Jared Wells against Minion; the second half was never posted.
